subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: No unit tests were added for the new ContentstackProvider component. The review criteria require that new features have corresponding unit tests mirroring the src/ path. The ContentstackProvider introduces live preview initialization, state management, and SDK callback subscription — all untested. The diff modified 30+ existing test files (import path changes only) but added zero new test files.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a test file (e.g., src/context/__tests__/ContentstackContext.spec.tsx) that verifies: (1) the provider renders children, (2) initial content is passed through context, (3) onEntryChange callback triggers a state update and re-render with new content, (4) cleanup calls unsubscribeOnEntryChange on unmount, (5) init failure is silently caught. Mock @contentstack/live-preview-utils with vi.fn()/jest.fn() for onEntryChange, unsubscribeOnEntryChange, and init.

issues.description: The useEffect that syncs defaultContent into state (lines 30-32) can overwrite live preview updates. If the parent component re-renders and passes a new defaultContent object reference (even with identical content), setContent(defaultContent) will replace the live-preview-patched content with the stale SSR/SSG content, discarding any in-flight live edits. This directly undermines acceptance criterion 5 (subsequent updates continue to arrive over time).
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the useEffect that syncs defaultContent on prop change, or guard it so it only runs on mount. Since useState already initializes with defaultContent, the only scenario where re-syncing is needed is if defaultContent genuinely changes after mount — in which case consider using a ref to track whether live preview has already applied updates and skip the overwrite.

issues.description: footer?: [any] uses untyped any without an explanatory comment, violating TypeScript strict compliance. This was pre-existing in the old contentstackContext.tsx but is carried forward into the new file.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace [any] with a proper type (e.g., [IContentstackFooter] if such an interface exists) or add an inline comment explaining why any is used: footer?: [any]; // TODO: define IContentstackFooter interface.
